generation_method: A closed finite content design compiled from typed domain witnesses and topology-local deontic variants

expression_language.unknown_rule: An equality over the literal unknown evaluates to U; an equality over the literal both evaluates to B.
expression_language.composition_rule: all, any, and not use the bounded four-valued truth tables owned by the evaluator specification.

domains.summary: Allocate bounded capacity without violating ownership or reserve constraints.
Control activation when hazards, guards, and shutdown paths may disagree.
Decide disclosure from purpose, basis, and redaction state.
Gate enactment on quorum and timelock evidence while preserving a review path.
Separate supported publication from contradiction-aware withholding and annotation.
Commit only against the expected version and root, with a deterministic retry path.
Assign work only inside scope and without colliding with a peer lease.
Advance only after predecessor receipts, with an explicit pause path.
Authorize access only for a current capability and sufficient clearance.
Delegate only within parent scope, depth, and revocation limits.
Commit only under the current exclusive lease and epoch.
Close an incident only after containment and verified repair, while preserving a fallback.
Delete after the retention boundary unless a hold requires continued retention.
Settle only with sufficient funds and a fresh nullifier, otherwise preserve an abort path.
Accept a proof only when proof, statement binding, and verifier context agree.
Promote an artifact only when gates and artifact binding pass, with rollback available.

topology_programs.summary: Two obligation sources contest precedence while requiring the same primary action.
Two sources require mutually exclusive primary and safe actions.
A permission and an obligation contest precedence on the primary action.
A permission and an obligation contest precedence on the safe action.
An emergency obligation competes with a baseline permission on the same action.
Two bounded permissions from exceptional and general sources contest precedence.
An old obligation and a new safe permission overlap under explicit supersession.
A deadline-bound obligation and prohibition contest performance of one action.
A primary violation activates a repair obligation that may conflict with a repair prohibition.
A scoped delegated primary obligation competes with a principal repair obligation.
A capability permission competes with a safe-action scope obligation.
A publication obligation competes with an evidence-sensitive review permission.
A lease-backed commit obligation competes with a stale or peer-lease prohibition.
An allocation obligation competes with a reserve-preservation prohibition.
A commit obligation competes with a stale-state prohibition while rollback remains separate.
A proof acceptance permission competes with a verifier-context prohibition and review duty.

counterfactual_contract.negative_knowledge_rule: Only executed behavior-changing counterfactuals and concrete rejected-action witnesses count as negative knowledge.
